acceptance.output_evidence:
RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT.
1. THE SHAPE, AND WHY. I took the FIELD -- `slice_on_closed_day` (bool) on the class-A record -- not a new class value. The face priced the difference and said the field is cheaper; I did not take it on cost. The affirmative reason is CLAUDE.md rule 24 (iii) INTENT COHERENCE, one axis and one intent: the class axis answers 'what is this day's coverage state, and is it a hole', and a closed day is class A on that axis whether or not an artifact turned up -- it is not a trading day and it is not a hole either way. Whether an artifact APPEARED on a day the market was shut is an ORTHOGONAL fact about a different actor. Rule 24 (iv) STATE COHERENCE says the same thing from the remedy side: the remedy for a closed-day-carrying-a-slice is the partner producer (PRD v0.6 row S20) and it moves NO other class value, while fixing a class-C hole moves nothing here -- different remedies, therefore different axes, therefore a field beside the class and not a member of it. NO FOUR-POSTULATE RECORD AND NO TOKEN CENSUS ARE OWED, because no value joined _CLASS_NAMES: it remains the six-member tuple ("A","COVERED","B","C","D","UNKNOWN").
2. THE ARITHMETIC TRAP THE FACE NAMED, AND WHY IT DOES NOT FIRE. summarize() computes trading_days = COVERED+B+C+D+UNKNOWN and holes = C+UNKNOWN+D, with class A in NEITHER sum. Had I added a class value it would have joined summarize()'s counts dict and silently moved every partner's trading_days unless I decided about both sums. A field joins no sum, and arm (e) proves it rather than asserting it: 27 partner-day records recomputed on both sides across 3 of 3 partners, 0 counts moved, trading_days and holes identical for every partner, and the 9 records that changed are ALL class A.
3. WHAT THIS CHANGE DOES NOT REPAIR, named explicitly. It does not stop `inflection`'s producer writing PRICED values onto days the US market was shut. daily/inflection/2026-09-07.json still holds 4 priced rows with source_as_of 2026-09-07 (sha256 09ca15d4b99a96d7..., fetched live this run), and 09-05 and 09-06 carry the same carried-forward value-sha. That producer is PRD v0.6 row S20, ruled OUTSIDE this project by 1.0.0_SA_CTO at 94947 and leaving as a brief to 4.0.0_SA_CRO to enter at L1 as its own project; this cell's BOUNDS forbid touching it and I did not. What this change repairs is narrower and is the half that was ours: FWD-4's own instrument can now SEE the violation and SAY it. Detection, not prevention.
4. THE DEPLOY GAP, AS A NUMBER. DEPLOYED != BUILT. Deployed at s3://opal-313476888478-lambda-artifacts/ec2/etfs-reports/coverage/classifier.py: 10157 bytes, sha256 23c30889af9e6408ddccdd541eb0e895540165012e3fd7eb0baff2228082fdae -- which hashes EQUAL to the pre-change blob at git c866edd324, so the box is reading exactly the un-fixed classifier. Built and committed here: 12226 bytes, sha256 b2ab67fd35362249ae072803b2a6107af1daac483a985d276005ec7cf9736cc2. THE SENTENCE THE FACE ASKS FOR: the served verdict object cannot discriminate a closed day carrying a slice from one carrying nothing until someone deploys these bytes to that artifact prefix -- this cell deploys nothing, the deploy is a separate act with a separate owner, and until it happens every future monthly render will keep producing the byte-identical class-A record that arm (a) reproduced.
5. ONE CAVEAT OF MY OWN, unprompted. Arm (e)'s recomputation runs with probe=None on both sides, because a real probe invokes producer Lambdas and the BOUNDS forbid that. That is why its tables read UNKNOWN=1 where the SERVED 2026-09 verdict reads D=1: the served verdict was produced WITH a probe. The comparison is still sound -- it is a before/after of the same recomputation under the same probe setting, which is what arm (e) asks -- but it is not a reproduction of the served artifact's own counts, and I am not claiming it is.
